problem: Top VLN-CE systems depend on depth, LiDAR, multi-camera rigs or maps, which limits which robots they run on and raises cost. Their metric-coordinate outputs also tie them to specific robot geometry, and per-timestep training on long episodes is extremely expensive.
motivation: A deployable navigation policy should minimize sensor assumptions, transfer across embodiments, and train cheaply from simulation alone. Monocular RGB is the most universal sensor, and image-space pointing is independent of camera intrinsics and scene scale.
key_idea: An 8B VLM that sees only monocular RGB predicts the next waypoint by pointing in the image (with a metric-displacement fallback). It is trained on 2.4M simulated trajectories with a prefix-tree attention mask that packs whole episodes into one sequence, then refined with online RL (CISPO).
insight: Online RL on a hard subset of failed SFT trajectories adds about 4 points SR: R2R-CE val-unseen goes from 73.40 to 77.43 and RxR-CE from 71.2 to 75.1. This suggests behavioral cloning of shortest paths lacks recovery behavior. The prefix-tree mask gives the same training signal as per-step samples with 22x fewer tokens, and it blocks leakage of ground-truth previous actions. No separate ablation of the pointing formulation or the data scale is reported.
method: Pointing waypoint prediction: the VLM outputs image coordinates (u,v) of the furthest visible waypoint plus the heading change Δθ, and co-predicts metric displacement (Δx,Δy,Δθ). When the goal is out of view it omits (u,v) and gives displacement only; it also emits STOP.

Diffusion action head: a 121M diffusion transformer takes the VLM waypoint, robot height and radius, the context frame and the current frame, and outputs 30 delta poses at 10 Hz. An embodiment-specific motion-tracking controller then produces 100 Hz motor commands.

Simulated data generation: 2.4M expert trajectories over 350k indoor and outdoor scenes, with farthest-point-sampled start/goal pairs, some spanning multiple floors. Robot height (0.4-1.8 m), radius, camera height and pitch are randomized.

Prefix-tree SFT: a whole episode I|O0|a0|...|On|an is packed into one sequence. A tree attention mask lets a token attend only to trunk tokens or tokens in its own branch, so previous GT actions are hidden. Token cost drops from O(T^2) to O(T), a 22x reduction.

Online RL with CISPO: reward is -max(2, geodesic dist to goal), which encourages STOP near the goal. It runs asynchronously with the simulator and vLLM generators. Training uses a 35k hard-task subset where SFT fails, packed by scene as a visual curriculum.
Initialization: an 8B VLM pretrained for spatial grounding (pointing, counting, localization), taking a history of RGB frames plus the instruction.

setting.backbone: Robostral 8B VLM (fine-tuned from a grounding-oriented dense 8B VLM) + 121M diffusion transformer policy
setting.training_data: 2.4M simulated trajectories over 350k scenes (Habitat/HM3D-style), SFT with prefix trees, then CISPO RL on a 35k hard-task subset
setting.observation: monocular RGB stream (single camera) plus instruction
setting.action_space: image-space pointing waypoint + heading change (metric displacement fallback), converted to 10 Hz trajectory chunks by diffusion policy; Habitat pathfinder used between waypoints in benchmark evaluation
setting.simulator: Habitat (training and evaluation); real robots Galaxea R1 and Hiwonder JetAuto for cross-embodiment demo
setting.privileged: none for the policy; Habitat pathfinder is used to move between predicted waypoints during benchmark evaluation

numbers.extra: SFT + CISPO RL; trained on 2.4M simulated trajectories; Habitat pathfinder between waypoints

numbers_note: Only SR is reported for the SFT-only variant and for val-seen. The RxR-CE SFT SR is 71.2 in text, and no full metrics were given for these variants. Table values are printed as fractions and were converted to percentages.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen it reaches SR 77.4 and SPL 74.2 with only monocular RGB, beating the best monocular Qwen-RobotNav-4B (66.9) by 10.5 and the best depth/multi-camera Qwen-RobotNav-8B (72.1) by 5.3. On RxR-CE it gets SR 75.1 and SPL 68.7, beating all monocular baselines and the depth-assisted models on SPL and NE, but trailing Qwen-RobotNav-8B with depth on SR (76.5).
limitations: No ablations for the pointing design, data scale or robot randomization; the paper reports only SFT vs RL.
Evaluation uses a Habitat pathfinder between waypoints instead of the full learned diffusion/controller stack, and real-robot results are only qualitative.
Technical report with few details on the base VLM and simulation assets, so it is hard to reproduce.
